title: s1: Simple test-time scaling
abstract: This paper introduces a simple approach to achieve test-time scaling and strong reasoning performance in language models. The authors propose a method called budget forcing, which controls the test-time compute by forcefully terminating the model's thinking process or lengthening it by appending 'Wait' to the model's generation.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a complex math problem. You can either think about it quickly and risk making a mistake, or take your time and increase your chances of getting it right. This is similar to how language models work, and the idea of test-time scaling is to give them more time to think and improve their performance.

We can think of this as a trade-off between speed and accuracy, where more test-time compute can lead to better results.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
The authors propose a method called budget forcing, which controls the test-time compute by forcefully terminating the model's thinking process or lengthening it by appending 'Wait' to the model's generation. This approach allows the model to reflect on its current generation and arrive at a better answer.

The process involves selecting a subset of 1,000 samples from a large dataset based on three guiding principles: quality, difficulty, and diversity.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
The authors evaluate their approach on three representative reasoning benchmarks: AIME24, MATH500, and GPQA Diamond. The results show that their model, s1-32B, outperforms other models and achieves state-of-the-art performance on these benchmarks.

The model achieves an accuracy of 57% on AIME24, 95% on MATH500, and 60% on GPQA Diamond.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
The approach proposed in this paper has significant implications for the field of natural language processing. It shows that test-time scaling can be achieved with a simple and efficient method, and that this approach can lead to state-of-the-art performance on reasoning benchmarks.

This work also highlights the importance of careful data selection and the need for diverse and high-quality datasets.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
The key innovation of this paper is the proposal of budget forcing, a simple and efficient method for controlling test-time compute. This approach allows the model to reflect on its current generation and arrive at a better answer.

The authors also propose a set of guiding principles for selecting a subset of samples from a large dataset, including quality, difficulty, and diversity.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
The authors provide an open-source implementation of their approach, including the model, data, and code. This allows researchers and practitioners to try out the approach and experiment with different settings and datasets.

The code is available at https://github.com/simplescaling/s1.
